items.question: Was the research published in a credible venue?

items.question: Do the researchers discuss limitations, threats to validity, assumptions, or scope boundaries?
items.rationale: The authors state multiple scope boundaries and assumptions, including omitted mission modes and omitted subsystems, simplified/worst-case assumptions, human expertise requirements, and future work needed for integration and evaluation.
evidence: "Only a subset of the CREME project's requirements and constraints is considered in this paper due to space constraints."
"Without loss of complexity, mission modes are not discussed in this paper."
"In the example presented in this paper, neither Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS), nor radiation or thermal considerations are included."

items.question: Is the nanosatellite/CubeSat mission context and lifecycle stage described clearly enough to interpret applicability?
items.rationale: The paper clearly situates the work in CubeSat concurrent preliminary/conceptual design and describes the CREME LEO radiation-monitoring CubeSat use case, payload, institutions, constraints, and iteration context.
evidence: "Nanospace is a web application dedicated to facilitate concurrent engineering during the preliminary design phase of CubeSats."
"Its objective is to measure the radiation environment in Low Earth Orbit (LEO)."
"As a simulation scenario, as a first step it will be verified whether a 2U CubeSat would be feasible in terms of power consumption"

items.question: Are the MBSE method, language, toolchain, model artifacts, and system boundary described clearly enough to support replication or comparison?
items.rationale: The paper identifies SysML, Nanospace, MB2DM, DSM/dependency artifacts, Python/GMAT/Dosa/Stela/CelestLab scripts, and the CubeSat system boundary, but the MBSE model contents, tool versions, algorithms, URLs, and exchange details are not sufficiently detailed for full replication.
evidence: "As an experiment, a CubeSat model was realised in a SysML tool, creating requirements diagrams, realising a functional diagram using the state machine diagram, then an internal block diagram was used, as well as internal diagrams for each subsystem using the parametric diagram."
"The open-source Nanospace framework [7] is a dedicated open-source concurrent design engineering tool, mainly consisting of a GUI, a database and an API"
"MBSE software connectivity does not come automatically and few models can be exchanged between software without information loss."

items.question: Are claimed outcomes explicitly linked to MBSE artifacts, MBSE activities, or model-enabled process changes rather than asserted generically?
items.rationale: Most claimed benefits are linked to MBSE artifacts or model-enabled processes such as SysML-derived DSMs, dependency graphs, Nanospace requirement flags, change propagation, traceability, reuse, and semi-automated analysis loops.
evidence: "MBSE can be used to capture the system dependencies represented in Figs.1 and 2, allowing to reuse knowledge from previous CubeSat missions."
"This paper shows how MBSE system models could enhance the propagation of parameter updates or changes on Nanospace, whether using parametric design structure matrices or dependency graphs."
"The main outcome of parametric DSMs from MBSE models could constitute a powerful tool that can be used to set a sequencing within the design steps with NanoSpace"

items.question: Is evidence provided for claimed outcomes, such as metrics, baseline comparison, case-study results, executable simulation results, model checks, stakeholder evaluation, reuse evidence, integration/test results, or flight/operational data?
items.rationale: The CREME scenario provides simulation outputs and constraint-check examples, including power/DoD plots and design iterations, but the broader MBSE value claims are not supported by baseline comparison, stakeholder evaluation, repeated reuse, integration testing, or flight data.
evidence: "Simulation allows for a first check on the order of magnitude of available power"
"Simulation shows that, in spite of heavy transceiver data burst, batteries are able to recharge see Fig. 4."
"Finally, it would be good to compare the performance of Nanospace with and without a MBSE vision"

items.question: Are requirements, verification, validation, design decisions, or lifecycle gates traced to model artifacts when such traceability is central to the paper?
items.rationale: Requirements and constraints are represented in tables and Nanospace, then related to dependency graphs, DSMs, and simulation checks, but there is no complete requirements-to-design-to-verification traceability model or lifecycle gate trace.
evidence: "Requirements (see table II) are set into Nanospace, and, depending on the known unknowns, design parameters are set as much as possible."
"The dependency graph (Fig. 1) or the design structure matrix (Fig. 2) are available to show the feedback loops and sequence of which part of the script should be re-run."
Fig. 5 caption: "Requirements concerning telecommunication aspects are not compliant yet."

items.question: Are model availability, open-source assets, reusable packages, data exchange mechanisms, or sufficient implementation details reported to assess reproducibility and toolchain continuity?
items.rationale: Open-source Nanospace, AGPL scripts, example input/output, APIs, and a data-flow concept are reported, but the Markdown lacks usable script/model URLs and the authors explicitly identify continuity and information-loss issues across tools.
evidence: "For CREME's preliminary design Python scripts were developed and used; they can be accessed here $ ^{1} $ under the AGPL v3 license."
"Nanospace allows for direct information exchange between third-party expert software"
"The lack of data continuity throughout the complete system life cycle is one of the biggest lacks of the mentioned CDE tools"

quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The paper is credible and context-rich, with clear CubeSat preliminary-design scope and concrete power/data/reentry simulations. Its main weakness for extraction is that MBSE-Nanospace integration is an early conceptual effort: model artifacts, algorithms, availability, formal traceability, and comparative evidence are only partially reported.

RQ1.rationale: The paper models a nanosatellite mission at system/preliminary-design level using requirements, constraints, simplified discipline parameters, dependency graphs, DSMs, and known-unknown assumptions; EPS is represented mainly through power-budget parameters rather than a full EPS behavioral model.

RQ2.rationale: It claims MBSE/Nanospace can improve reuse, traceability, consistency, communication, time/cost, and integrability/data continuity, but the claims are mostly system-level and conceptual rather than EPS-specific or empirically demonstrated.

RQ3.rationale: Pre-physical simulations and Nanospace requirement flags check power/DoD, data, link-budget, and reentry constraints; however, verification is not presented as a formal integrated EPS model-based verification procedure.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: No other papers or prior extractions were consulted. This extraction treats the study as part of the Nanospace/CREME CubeSat preliminary-design line, with MBSE integration still in an early research stage.

Dependency graph and design structure matrix for design-parameter interactions

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_level_of_abstraction: System-level CubeSat mission and subsystem preliminary design; discipline-level parameters and constraints rather than detailed component, circuit, or high-fidelity behavioral models.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_modeling: Only a subset of CREME requirements/constraints is used; mission modes are omitted; ADCS, radiation, and thermal considerations are omitted from the example; circular orbit and worst-case assumptions are used; scripts are described as simple pedagogical preliminary-design analysis.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Some orbital mechanics and CubeSat design expertise is required for choices such as SSO inclination, RAAN worst-case selection, margins, available flight-proven technology, platform power estimates, and trade-offs when constraints fail.

RQ1: A general CubeSat preliminary-design model can be built from simplified discipline inputs/outputs, requirements, constraints, dependency graphs, and DSMs, with EPS represented by power-budget parameters such as payload/platform power, eclipse duration, solar panels, batteries, and DoD.

The approach explicitly accommodates limited behavioral knowledge through known unknowns, margins, expert estimates, worst-case assumptions, and modular dependencies that can later add mission modes or omitted subsystems.
RQ2: Claimed MBSE/Nanospace outcomes include improved communication, information sharing, traceability, reuse, consistency, system understanding, time/cost reduction, and data continuity, but evidence is mostly conceptual and system-level.
Reproducibility/accessibility is supported by open-source Nanospace and AGPL scripts, but model and URL details are incomplete in the Markdown, limiting independent assessment.
RQ3: Pre-physical verification is demonstrated mainly through semi-automated scripts and Nanospace requirement flags: DoD, power generation, contact time, link budget, data rate, and reentry constraints are checked before hardware development.
The EPS-related verification is not a fully integrated SysML/EPS V&V procedure; it is a database/API-linked preliminary simulation and constraint-checking workflow.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Only a subset of CREME requirements and constraints is considered due to space constraints.
ADCS, radiation, and thermal considerations are excluded from the example.
The process remains semi-automatic and requires human expertise.
MBSE software connectivity does not come automatically and model exchange can lose information.
Manual dependency-graph construction is counter-intuitive and MB2DM/Nanospace UI integration needs further development.
Nanospace database structure needs reassessment to include parameter details and relations.
Future work should compare Nanospace performance with and without an MBSE vision.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: Venue name is not visible in the Markdown and is not supplied in the metadata beyond IEEE DOI/paperId.
The SysML model, DSM-generation algorithm details, and repository URLs are insufficiently reported for full replication.
MBSE value claims lack baseline comparison, quantified outcome metrics, stakeholder evaluation, reuse evidence, integration testing, or operational/flight data.
EPS is treated as a power-budget/electrical-architecture concern, not as a detailed EPS architecture or behavioral MBSE model.
Traceability from requirements to model elements, analyses, and verification artifacts is illustrative but not complete or formalized.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: Nanospace is a web application dedicated to facilitate concurrent engineering during the preliminary design phase of CubeSats.
Nanospace may benefit from MBSE, as MBSE facilitates knowledge reuse; which could allow a faster design convergence and faster inspection of candidate architectures.
Only a subset of the CREME project's requirements and constraints is considered in this paper due to space constraints.
Without loss of complexity, mission modes are not discussed in this paper.
In the example presented in this paper, neither Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS), nor radiation or thermal considerations are included.
MBSE can be used to capture the system dependencies represented in Figs.1 and 2, allowing to reuse knowledge from previous CubeSat missions.
